ledger.note: 1213: Archbishop Eberhard II is made a prince of the Empire. The page gives no year for secular rule beyond this and the late-13th-century immediacy ('gradually reached the status of Imperial immediacy and independence from the Bavarian dukes'); the infobox and the disambiguation page date the secular jurisdiction 1328-1803 ('State constitution' 1328). The dossier starts at 1213, the year of the princely title.

ledger.note: 1275: the Rupertiwinkel acknowledged. 'The episcopal territory was acknowledged by Duke Louis II of Bavaria, in the course of Salzburg's elevation to a prince-archbishopric' (Rupertiwinkel page). The page also dates a Bavarian grant of Piding to Rupert c. 700 and the foundation of Höglwörth Abbey in 1125, which are not territorial events of the principality. [Reviewer eu-08-x, 2026-10-25: counterpart corrected from stem-duchy-of-bavaria, which ends in 1255; Louis II of Bavaria ruled Upper Bavaria, the Cliopatria Duchy of Bavaria (duchy-of-bavaria) from 1255/1260]

ledger.note: 1803: secularised. 'Salzburg was secularised as the Electorate of Salzburg' for Ferdinand III (Prince-Archbishopric page). Prince-Archbishop Colloredo resigned on 11 February 1803 and two weeks later the territory was secularised (Electorate page); the electorate lasted until the Peace of Pressburg of 26 December 1805.

wars.name: Wolf Dietrich's invasion of Berchtesgaden
wars.outcome: 'In October 1611 his forces invaded the Berchtesgaden Provostry,' which the Wittelsbach also claimed; 'in the subsequent clashes of arms, Bavarian troops campaigned in Salzburg'; the archbishop fled to Carinthia and was captured, deposed and imprisoned for life by his nephew Mark Sittich von Hohenems (infobox term ends 7 March 1612).
wars.note: The page says nothing about the outcome of the Berchtesgaden claim; no border change is drawn.

notes: Five pages opened (one is the disambiguation page; the Eberhard II pages failed to load). The pages disagree on the start: 1213 (Eberhard II made a prince), late 13th century (immediacy) and 1328 (infobox, 'secular jurisdiction between 1328 and 1803'); the dossier starts at 1213, the earliest dated princely act, with confidence 2. The secular territory is drawn as the modern Land of Salzburg because the page calls it 'roughly congruent'; the pages date no acquisition inside it and say nothing of Friesach, Gastein, the Zillertal or other exclaves, so none is drawn. The Rupertiwinkel is drawn from 1275 only because that is the only dated acknowledgement. Not settled: the outcome of the 1611 Berchtesgaden clash, the end of the 1800 occupation, Colloredo's end year (the succession list gives 1772-1812; the text and the Electorate page give 1803).
